entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16160"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 22</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Acts.22.1-Acts.22.30">Ac 22:1-30</reference>. Paul's Defense from the Stairs of the Fortress--The Rage of the Audience Bursting Forth, the Commandant Has Him Brought into the Fort to Be Examined by Scourging, but Learning that He Is a Roman, He Orders His Release and Commands the Sanhedrin to Try Him.</title> <div sID="gen31253" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16160"/><hi type="bold">2. when they heard ... the Hebrew tongue--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Acts.21.40">Ac 21:40</reference>).<div eID="gen31253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31254" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they kept the more silence--</hi>They could have understood him in Greek, and doubtless fully expected the renegade to address them in that language, but the sound of their holy mother tongue awed them into deeper silence. <div eID="gen31254" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 17-21. it came to pass, &c.-- This thrilling dialogue between the glorified Redeemer and his chosen vessel is nowhere else related. when I was come again to Jerusalem-- on the occasion mentioned in Ac 9:26-29 . while I prayed in the temple-- He thus calls their attention to the fact that after his conversion he kept up his connection with the temple as before.
